subject: Questions on data use: training & deletion procedures

Subject: Questions on data use: training and deletion procedures

Hi Priyom / Rachel,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — PayGrid is very interested in Redwood for a transaction-class use case. Before we go deeper on sizing and procurement we'd like clear, written answers to a few compliance questions to brief our internal security and legal teams:

1) Do you ever use customer request/response content to train or fine-tune Redwood models (either internal research or public releases)?
2) What are your default retention windows for request logs, generated outputs, and audit logs?
3) If we ask for data deletion, what is the exact process and how do you prove deletion (audit IDs, timelines)?

Can you also attach any SOC2 summary and your DPA? Our security team wants the docs up front.

Best,
Alice Turner

alice.turner@paygrid.com

Hi Alice — great to hear PayGrid found the demo useful. Short answers up front, details below and I'm attaching the SOC2 summary + our standard DPA.

- Training: We do not train or fine-tune our production models on customer input by default. Customer content sent to the hosted Redwood API is not incorporated into model weights or used to train public models unless a customer explicitly opts into a training program in writing.

- Retention: Default operational windows are: full request/response payloads retained for 30 days for debugging/quality reasons; short-term traces and metrics retained 7 days; audit logs (auth/connectivity) retained 365 days by default. For Dedicated/Private deployments, retention is controlled by the customer or contract terms.

- Deletion: Customers can request immediate deletion via our support portal or their account rep. Deletion requests generate an internal Deletion Request ID and include the scope (timestamps, API keys, specific resources). We mark data for deletion (tombstone) within 24 hours and scrub active storage; backups are swept on the next scheduled backup retention purge (typical window 60-90 days depending on the backup tier). We will provide a signed confirmation containing the Deletion Request ID and the storage objects removed.

A few nuances and operational notes:
- Telemetry/aggregates: We collect aggregated telemetry (error rates, latency histograms) for product health; these are anonymized, aggregated, and are not reversible to original customer content.
- Support snapshots: At times support/SEs may capture snippets for debugging; these are treated as operational artifacts and are managed under the same deletion process when requested.
- Private deployments: On VPC/on-prem installations customers retain control over data residency and deletion; Redwood acts only as the control plane unless otherwise contracted.

I'm looping in Mina from Trust & Safety for confirmation on the deletion playbook and the evidence format we provide to customers.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary_v3.pdf, DPA_Redwood_Inference_2026.docx

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if security wants to run through specifics.

—Priyom

Thanks Priyom — that helps. A couple of follow-ups from our security team:

1) Can you confirm whether any of the aggregated telemetry could be used to reconstruct PII or transaction payloads? Our rule is no reversible telemetry.
2) For the deletion confirmation, can you share a sample of the confirmation file/schema? We need something our auditors can reconcile (timestamp, deletion id, objects removed).

Finally — does Redwood offer an SLA or contractual language guaranteeing deletion timelines (e.g., completed within X days)? If not, we'd need to include expected timelines in the DPA/contract.

Appreciate it,
Alice
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>

Hi Alice — Mina on Trust & Safety. Quick answers + sample deletion confirmation below.

1) Re telemetry: we do not generate any telemetry that is reversible to raw request/response payloads. Aggregates are computed as numeric metrics (counts, percentiles) and do not include snippets or identifiers that would allow reconstruction of PII or full transaction bodies. If a customer requires additional safeguards we can disable telemetry collection for their org or configure strict sampling via Dedicated/Private deployment options.

2) Deletion confirmation schema (sample):
- deletion_request_id: DR-20270209-8891
- customer_org: PayGrid
- scope: api_keys, request_payloads between 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z and 2027-02-09T00:00:00Z
- requested_by: Alice Turner <alice.turner@paygrid.com>
- requested_at: 2027-02-09T12:41:05Z
- actions_taken:
  - tombstone_marked: 2027-02-09T12:42:12Z
  - active_storage_scrubbed: 2027-02-09T12:50:47Z
  - backup_retention_window: next scheduled purge (expected completion by 2027-04-09)
- delivered_by: trustops@redwoodinference.com (signed)

Process / timelines:
- Step 1: Customer opens a Data Erasure Request via support or your account rep (we create Deletion Request ID within 24h).
- Step 2: Engineering performs active storage scrub (usually completes within 48 hours for scoped data).
- Step 3: Backups are swept according to backup retention policy — typical purge window 60-90 days; we provide expected purge date in the confirmation.
- Step 4: We deliver a signed confirmation PDF and a machine-readable JSON schema blob that your auditors can ingest (example fields above).

Contract language: we can include a deletion SLA in the DPA for Dedicated/Enterprise customers (e.g., active-storage scrub within 5 business days, backups removed within N days). For hosted tier this is typically stated as "best efforts" in the standard DPA, but we will negotiate firm timelines for an enterprise contract.

I'll also attach a short checklist we use internally and can share as an appendix to the DPA. If you'd like, we can convert the sample confirmation into a CSV/JSON schema for your audit tooling.
